scope: Implement only the accepted MU Desk File Shelf (file-shelf) module, its edge-docked WPF drag-and-drop surface, local path-metadata persistence, and the minimum existing host/settings/tray integration required by the accepted contracts.

owned_files.change: Add the pure settings contract for enabled state, left/right dock side, display device name, and clamped relative vertical position.
Add versioned shelf, batch, item, removal snapshot, type, order, pin, and validation models with a hard 200-path limit and no file-content fields.
Add atomic JSON load/save with temporary replacement, one last-known-good backup, recovery result reporting, rollback-safe mutation, and injectable paths for deterministic tests.
Add one FileShelf settings section and normalize missing legacy fields while preserving all existing defaults and serialized properties.
Add the single IToolModule coordinator owning enable, pause, show/collapse, item count, persistence, one-session undo, one-window lifetime, errors, and state events.
Add the accepted dark-translucent collapsed tab and 320 px expanded grouped shelf with empty, valid/invalid drag, missing-path, save-error, pin, remove, clear, undo, and keyboard states.

Handle external FileDrop validation/grouping, standard drag-out, successful-result cleanup for unpinned items, group and item actions, focus behavior, auto-expand, collapse, per-monitor placement, DPI, and reduced motion.
Add minimal Win32 helpers for no-taskbar edge-window styles, non-activating drag approach, monitor work-area lookup, and display/DPI-safe placement; no shell hook or global mouse hook.
Add only keyed File Shelf tab, panel, batch, row, drag-target, missing, and focus resources using inherited MU tokens.
Produce and package the accepted shelf-board, file-tabs, and violet-drop-point module icon at 16, 20, 24, 32, 64, 128, and 256 px after authorization.
Package File Shelf icon resources only; add no database, Shell extension, background service, or third-party runtime dependency.
Update the real tool count from five to six and add one peer two-column File Shelf card with toggle, true item count, and Show/Collapse action without restyling unrelated cards.
Accept the FileShelfModule, expose enabled-change and show/collapse actions, and refresh its running, paused, visibility, and item-count state.
Add one MU Desk-owned File Shelf command, include its checked state in the existing tray refresh, and update the started notice without creating a second icon or notification path.
Construct and start one FileShelfModule, wire settings/tray/home/pause/shutdown/error flows, and dispose it while preserving current single-instance and all existing module behavior.

Add deterministic default/normalization, validation, 200-item cap, same-drop grouping, pin behavior, successful/failed drag-out mutation, atomic save, backup recovery, rollback, privacy, and legacy-settings tests.

technical_route.drag_in: WPF AllowDrop over a topmost edge window; accept only DataFormats.FileDrop values that resolve to existing local file-system files or directories at drop time; reject virtual files, text URLs, and non-file data.
technical_route.drag_out: WPF DragDrop.DoDragDrop with a standard FileDrop DataObject advertising copy/link-compatible effects but never deleting, moving, or renaming the source path; remove unpinned metadata only when Windows returns a non-None result.
technical_route.window: One borderless WPF window inside MU Desk, collapsed to an edge tab and expanded in place; Windows monitor work-area and per-monitor DPI determine clamped placement.
technical_route.icons: Reuse Windows Shell small file-type icons at runtime and the accepted MU module icon for the host/tab; no content thumbnails or persistent icon cache.
technical_route.storage: Versioned JSON under %LocalAppData%/MU Desk/file-shelf using temp write, atomic replace, one backup, and in-memory rollback on failure.
technical_route.runtime_weight: No database, file watcher, polling worker, clipboard listener, Shell extension, browser component, network client, child process, or independent updater.

preserve: MU Desk remains the single process, user entry, tray, startup item, settings owner, version, About surface, and package.
Quick Ring, Dynamic Capture, CISP Question Bank, Cursor Gallery, Desktop Organizer, startup, single-instance activation, and current tray actions remain behaviorally unchanged.
Existing Toolbox settings deserialize with new File Shelf defaults and keep every previous value.
No original file or directory is copied into MU Desk, moved, renamed, deleted, content-read, indexed, uploaded, or logged by the module.
Disabling, pausing, resetting, upgrading, uninstalling normally, or removing File Shelf wiring does not delete source paths or silently clear shelf metadata.
A failed drop-in write, failed/cancelled drag-out, missing path, unavailable drive, or corrupt store never appears as successful state.
migrations: Legacy settings without FileShelf deserialize to enabled=true, right dock, primary display fallback, and vertical position 0.50 without rewriting unrelated values.
Create %LocalAppData%/MU Desk/file-shelf lazily on the first successful shelf mutation, not merely when MU Desk starts.
When shelf.json is absent, start with an empty shelf and no error; do not generate demo entries.
When shelf.json is valid but from an older supported schema, normalize optional fields in memory and write the new schema only on the next explicit mutation.
When the primary store is invalid, read shelf.json.bak without overwriting the corrupt primary until the user performs a successful mutation.
Never import, enumerate, move, or delete arbitrary recent files, clipboard history, downloads, desktop files, or previous module data.
implementation_sequence: Add File Shelf settings/models/store in Toolbox.Core and deterministic tests for normalization, limits, atomic persistence, backup recovery, rollback, and legacy settings.
Implement FileShelfModule lifecycle and prove empty start, enable/disable, pause/resume, single-window reuse, item counts, session undo, and sanitized errors without UI polish.
Build the borderless edge window and placement interop; verify right/left docking, work-area clamping, taskbar avoidance, primary-screen fallback, and 100/150/200 percent DPI.
Implement external FileDrop validation, same-drop batching, persistence commit, duplicate-path handling within a batch, missing-path states, and the 200-item cap.

Implement item/group drag-out using standard FileDrop, copy/link-compatible advertised effects, metadata cleanup only after a non-None result, pinned retention, failure restoration, remove, clear, and undo.
Apply the accepted light-outlined home card and dark-translucent shelf states, keyboard/focus support, reduced motion, system file icons, and no-content-preview rule.
Wire ToolboxSettings, App, MainWindow, tray, pause, startup, shutdown, errors, and update the real home tool count while preserving all existing module paths.
Produce and integrate the accepted File Shelf module icon family, validate small sizes, and retain a code-native fallback.

Run clean tests/build/publish, functional Explorer and cross-application drag checks, persistence/recovery/privacy checks, visual/accessibility checks, representative regression paths, and record evidence in acceptance.md.

risks.risk: A topmost edge window could obstruct applications or unexpectedly take focus.
risks.mitigation: Keep the idle hit area limited to the accepted tab, use non-activating drag approach behavior, enter keyboard focus only after explicit click/home/tray opening, and test taskbar/full-screen boundaries.

risks.risk: WPF OLE drag-and-drop behavior differs across Explorer, browsers, editors, elevated applications, and virtual-file sources.
risks.mitigation: Support only standard FileDrop paths, show concrete rejection for virtual sources, test Explorer plus representative target apps, and never claim universal support or success before the returned effect.

risks.risk: A target application could interpret a drag in a way that surprises the user.
risks.mitigation: Advertise copy/link-compatible effects rather than Move, never call file operations from MU Desk, describe completion as '已拖出' rather than copied/moved, and retain pinned metadata.

risks.risk: Removing metadata immediately on mouse release could lose the shelf entry when the target rejects the drop.
risks.mitigation: Keep an in-place placeholder during DoDragDrop and commit removal only after a non-None result and a successful atomic store write; otherwise restore the row.

risks.risk: Monitor topology, taskbar position, negative coordinates, and per-monitor DPI can place or blur the shelf incorrectly.
risks.mitigation: Use monitor work areas and effective coordinates, persist relative vertical position, clamp every show/topology change, and test left/right/above primary displays at 100, 150, and 200 percent.

risks.risk: Paths may become unavailable or expose private project/customer names through logs.
risks.mitigation: Check availability only on display/drag, retain explicit unavailable rows, sanitize diagnostics to counts/stages/random IDs, and never log full paths or filenames.

risks.risk: A write failure or corrupt JSON could silently lose a shelf containing many paths.
risks.mitigation: Use temp plus atomic replace, one known-good backup, validate before commit, rollback in-memory mutations, preserve corrupt files, and test simulated I/O and malformed JSON failures.

risks.risk: Default-enabled upgrade behavior could feel intrusive.
risks.mitigation: Start strictly collapsed at the accepted 36 px edge profile, never steal focus or notify, expose an immediate card toggle, and ensure pause/disable removes the edge window completely.

build: Release build and Toolbox, MouseRing, and DesktopOrganizer tests pass from a clean process start.
Published output contains one MU Desk executable and File Shelf assets, with no module executable, database, service, Shell extension, file watcher dependency, or network client.
core_tests: Legacy settings gain valid FileShelf defaults while every prior value remains unchanged.
Dock side, device name, and vertical position normalize safely, including NaN/out-of-range input.
One drop creates one ordered batch; invalid/duplicate inputs are reported deterministically and total entries never exceed 200.
Pinned items survive successful drag-out; unpinned items are removed only after a simulated non-None result; None/cancel leaves all items unchanged.
Remove, clear-unpinned, and one-session undo mutate metadata only and never call file deletion or movement.
Atomic save leaves the last reliable shelf intact on simulated failure and backup recovery preserves valid items without overwriting corrupt evidence.
Serialized data contains only accepted metadata fields; sanitized diagnostics omit absolute paths and filenames.
drag_and_shelf_flow: Start with an empty store: MU Desk shows one collapsed edge tab, no expanded panel, no focus steal, no data folder creation, and a true zero count.
Drag one file, one folder, and a three-item selection from Explorer; verify exact grouping, order, names, type icons, item count, and persistence after MU Desk restart.
Drag a virtual browser item, text URL, nonexistent path, inaccessible path, and a selection exceeding the cap; verify rejection and no false saved state.
Drag one item and one whole batch to Explorer and representative accepting apps; verify returned-result handling, unpinned cleanup, pinned retention, and no source deletion/move by MU Desk.
Cancel over the desktop or use a rejecting target; verify the placeholder restores and copy reads '仍在货架上'.
Disconnect/reconnect a removable or network location and verify unavailable state, no automatic removal, and recovery on the next explicit check.
Disable, re-enable, pause, resume, show, collapse, tray-open, home-open, repeated-open, and shutdown; verify one window and correct persisted state throughout.
visual_and_accessibility: Inspect the sixth home card, tool count, collapsed tab, expanded shelf, groups, rows, empty, valid/invalid drag, missing, persistence error, undo, and clear confirmation against accepted contracts.
At 100, 150, and 200 percent scaling on available monitor arrangements, the shelf stays inside the work area, avoids the taskbar, remains sharp, and clamps safely after a monitor disappears.
Keyboard can open/collapse, traverse rows, pin, remove, clear, undo, and escape without deleting data; focus remains visible and every icon control has an accessible name.
High contrast and reduced motion preserve all information and functions; no status relies only on translucency, animation, or violet color.
The final module icon is legible at 16, 20, 24, and 32 px and uses the accepted shelf/file-tabs/violet-drop-point metaphor.
privacy_and_recovery: Monitor process/network behavior while idle and dragging: no child process, file watcher, clipboard listener, directory scan, content read, upload, or network request occurs.
Inspect settings, shelf JSON, backup, logs, and published output: paths exist only in accepted shelf metadata/error UI and never in logs or telemetry.
Simulate disk full, access denied, malformed primary JSON, malformed backup, atomic replace failure, and path disappearance; each remains visible and never produces false success or silent clearing.
Reset settings preserves shelf entries; clear-data confirmation states that originals remain; ordinary upgrade/publish does not remove the local shelf root.
Quick Ring, Dynamic Capture, CISP Question Bank, Cursor Gallery, Desktop Organizer, startup, tray pause/exit, and single-instance activation pass representative smoke paths.

rollback_and_recovery: All new user metadata is isolated under %LocalAppData%/MU Desk/file-shelf and no existing module data is moved, renamed, or deleted.
If the edge window cannot initialize, disable only File Shelf for the session, keep MU Desk and every other module operational, and surface the real error through the unified tray channel.
If the store cannot load, preserve primary and backup files, keep an explicit in-memory empty/error state, and offer the data location rather than overwriting evidence.
If a mutation cannot persist, restore the last reliable in-memory shelf and keep source paths untouched.
Removing File Shelf wiring from a future build leaves shelf.json as readable local JSON and leaves every referenced source file or folder exactly where it was.
